A train consists of 3 carriages chained together with links. Below shows a simple illustration: #####-#####-#####

Write a python class named Train with the following attributes:

Class Variable total stores total number of carriages

Object Variable name stores a name of the train

Functions input_name() ask user to input a name for the train it will also add the number of carriages to total display() displays name and total in a row

Write a program to create an 3 objects from the class. For each object, call input_name() followed by display().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

Alpha Bravo Charlie

Delta Echo Foxtrot

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Train name: Alpha Alpha 3 Train name: Bravo Bravo 6 Train name: Charlie Charlie 9

Example 2 Train name: Delta Delta 3 Train name: Echo Echo 6 Train name: Foxtrot Foxtrot 9

A train consists of carriages chained together with links. Each carriage is repsented by "#####" and a link is represented by "-". The example below shows a train with 3 carriages: #####-#####-#####

Write a python class named Train with the following attributes:

Class Variable total stores total number of carriages

Object Variable num stores the number of carriages making the train

Functions input_num() ask user to input a the number of carriages and save to num it will also add the number of carriages to total. display() displays the train formed with "#" and "-" as illustrated above                  and the total number of carriages

Write a program to create an 3 objects from the class. For each object, call input_num() followed by display().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

2 3 2

3 5 1

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Number of carriages: 2 #####-##### total carriages 2 Number of carriages: 3 #####-#####-##### total carriages 5 Number of carriages: 2 #####-##### total carriages 7

Example 2 Number of carriages: 3 #####-#####-##### total carriages 3 Number of carriages: 5 #####-#####-#####-#####-##### total carriages 8 Number of carriages: 1 ##### total carriages 9

A train consists of carriages chained together with links. The carriages can have different sizes. Each carriage is represented by a series of "#" and a link is represented by a "-". In the example below, there are 3 carriages of sizes 5, 3 and 4 forming the train: #####-###-####

Write a python class named Train with the following attributes:

Class Variable total_carriage stores total number of carriages total_size stores total size of all the carriages

Object Variable carriage_list stores a list of carriage sizes forming the train

Functions input_list() ask user to input a list of carriage sizes (from 1 to 10) and save to carriage_list it will also update total_carriage and total_size. display() displays the following: 1. the train formed with "#" and "-" as illustrated above 2. total_carriage 3. total_size

Write a program to create 2 objects from the class. For each object, call input_list() followed by display().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

5 5 5 4 3 5 1 6

3 6 1 6 9 6 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Input carriage sizes (1- 10): 5 5 5 #####-#####-##### total carriages 3 total size 15 Input carriage sizes (1- 10): 4 3 5 1 6 ####-###-#####-#-###### total carriages 8 total size 34

Example 2 Input sizes (1- 10): 3 6 1 ###-######-# total carriages 3 total size 10 Input carriage sizes(1- 10): 6 9 6 2 ######-#########-######-## total carriages 7 total size 33
